title: Session Variant Lab Notes: lightweight fidelity modes
content:
Quick brain-dump / scratchpad for "session variant" idea — aim: let apps pick an economical fidelity profile per session or switch mid-session.

Context:
- We need levers for customers to tune cost/latency vs. answer fidelity without changing prompts or models.
- Related: cost ladder fallbacks, progressive fidelity, snapshot stitching ideas floating around.

Problem statement (informal):
- Customers want deterministic cost ceilings and predictable latency for long conversations, but sometimes need high-fidelity answers for specific turns. Current approach is all-or-nothing: either run high-cost model or degrade quality across the whole session.

Goal: lightweight session-level profiles (variants) that map to a set of runtime behaviors: model variant, kv-cache retention policy, quantization hint, prefix-caching policy, batching priority.

Non-goals:
- Not building a full orchestration DSL yet. Keep surface minimal: attach a single `session_variant` tag at session-start or via an SDK call.

User stories (early):
- As a product engineer, I can start a session with `session_variant: economize` so the first N turns use low-cost routing and reduced kv retention.
- As an agent app, I can upgrade a session to `session_variant: deep` for critical question turns; runtime performs a best-effort warmup and routes to higher-tier model for subsequent tokens.
- As a monitoring owner, I can see per-variant token cost and latency breakdown in Console.

Examples of variants (sketch):
- economize: low-cost model fallback, low kv retention (evict older turns aggressively), batch-friendly (higher batching window), aggressive prefix compression.
- balanced: default, standard kv retention, normal batching.
- fidelity: high-quality model, keep more KV (longer retention), smaller batch windows, prefetch weights/warmups where possible.
- transient-boost: temporary fidelity bump for next X turns or Y seconds, then auto-reverts.

Acceptance criteria (rough):
- API: SDK call to start session supports `session_variant` string and optional `variant_ttl` (seconds or turns).
- Server: routing policy accepts variant and attempts to map to model pool + scheduling hint. Fallbacks documented.
- Observability: Console chart showing variant churn (sessions started per variant) + cost delta per variant.
- Behavior: transient-boost reverts automatically without user action.

API sketch (really rough):
- start_session({user_id, session_variant: "economize", variant_ttl: 600}) -> session_id
- update_session_variant(session_id, "fidelity", {turns: 3})
- session metadata in request headers: X-Session-Variant: fidelity

UX flows / UX notes:
- Developer experience should be minimal: a string enum most of the time. Provide presets in Console: "Economize", "Balanced", "Fidelity", "Boost".
- Offer a small JS SDK helper that toggles variant for a session and exposes current variant as session metadata.
- Consider a quick toggle in Conversation Inspector to force a transient-boost for repro/testing.

Rollout plan (idea-stage):
- internal dogfood in 2 weeks: add SDK + minimal server mapping for `economize` and `fidelity` to existing model pools (no infra changes).
- measure (1 week): token cost delta, p50/p95 latency, success rate for deep-turns (via eval snippets).
- iterate: add transient-boost and per-turn TTLs if metrics look good.

Metrics / success criteria:
- primary: average tokens-per-session cost reduction for sessions that choose economize >= 12% (vs baseline).
- safety: fidelity sessions do not regress quality by >2% on eval set.
- adoption: >10 internal teams try variants in dogfood within 4 weeks.

Operational considerations / tech notes: (brainstorm/low fidelity)
- routing: map variant -> (pool_tag, schedule_hint, cache_policy). Use existing smart-routing table with new columns.
- caching: variant can set kv_retention_seconds or kv_eviction_policy (LRU vs time-based). Implementation may be an approximation (we already evict by token count; add TTL is doable).
- batching: variant could set a batching window hint; need SRE input — larger windows help cost but increase latency. econ -> larger window. fidelity -> smaller window.
- model warmup: for transient-boost, attempt short warm-up (prefetch weights or spin-up) but keep fallback path. Might piggyback on dedicated capacity bursts if available.
- security: variants are just routing hints; no new data plane changes. Keep them in metadata only.

Open questions / unknowns (todo):
- granularity: session-only vs per-turn. Do we allow per-turn explicit overrides? (I like session-level + transient-boost for simplicity).
- UX: how verbose should Console presets be? Names will bias usage ("economize" sounds cheap). Need marketing/product review.
- billing: should we expose variant-specific per-token pricing? or keep billing unchanged but show expected savings?
- developer signals: how to surface variant falls back (e.g., if fidelity routing fails because no capacity, should we auto-fallback to balanced and send an event?).
- metrics: what eval set do we use to measure fidelity regressions? reuse existing micro-evals? create a tiny focused set for this feature.

Notes-to-self (todo bullets):
- sketch SDK patch: add startSessionVariant / updateSessionVariant helpers (JS + Python).
- wire up Console: quick toggle + table for variant usage (mocked for dogfood).
- short-lab experiment: create 10 synthetic sessions where we flip to fidelity on turn 5 and measure response quality vs baseline.
- ping SRE (mika) about safe batching window defaults and whether we can accept variant-based batching hints.
- draft short Confluence page for product review. Link to dogfood issue RI-4823.

Fragments / half-thoughts:
- Could reuse quality-monitoring + rollouts infra to detect if fidelity variant is regressing and auto-quarantine it.
- Maybe variants should be extensible metadata so advanced customers can add custom keys (but keep UI simple).

Slack crumbs: see thread #session-variants (pin later).

Next steps (this week):
- write minimal Confluence draft + attach this scratchpad (Isla)
- PR: add session_variant field to start_session SDK stub (Isla -> small branch)
- Dogfood: ask 3 internal teams to try economize on low-traffic bots (Rohan to coordinate)

Timestamped note (11/06): Rohan -> thumbs up on concept, suggests adding a "graceful degrade" option where fidelity sessions automatically enable compressed streaming to save tokens on long outputs.

End of scratchpad — will clean up into a proto-PRD if dogfood metrics look promising.
